version_note:
Corrects two metadata defects in version 1.0.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23101903). The scientific content, code, archive and results are unchanged; this is a metadata-only correction, which is why the minor version is not bumped past 2.0.0.

1. REFERENCES. In 1.0.0 the references field was published as 722 array entries of one character each, rather than the four intended citations. The source metadata held the citations as a single concatenated string, and Zenodo iterated it into characters. Nothing reported the error: a 722-element array of one-character strings is valid JSON, so the upload and every later read both appeared successful. The four citations are recoverable and are correct here.

2. SUBJECTS. In 1.0.0 the record carries zero subjects. Six free-text subject strings were supplied, but Zenodo requires controlled-vocabulary identifiers and silently discards free text. The six identifiers here were looked up in Zenodo's live vocabulary rather than guessed.

Both defects were found by inspecting the published record rather than trusting the upload. Version 1.0.0 remains published and is not withdrawn: it is the citable record for the scientific content. Cite this version for the corrected metadata.
notes:
NO AI SYSTEM WAS SCORED AND NO CLAIM IS MADE ABOUT AI CONSCIOUSNESS. This work builds and audits an instrument for measuring candidate indicators of consciousness in AI systems; it does not apply that instrument to any system, including the authors' own. It scores no model and no person.

Calibration status: 6 of 6 known-answer anchors pass. The battery is calibrated against published indicator properties, not against a ground truth of consciousness, which does not exist. Passing calibration means internal consistency, not correctness.

One methodological limit is stated openly and is not resolved: the aggregation temperature used by the battery was chosen by sweeping the same six anchors used to validate it, whose bands are themselves laboratory assumptions. Passing calibration therefore demonstrates internal consistency only. No absolute credence produced by this battery is a measurement; only ranking under shared assumptions is defensible.

Robustness was assessed over 3000 joint perturbations. One control fails by design and is reported as failing: an absolute performance ceiling does not hold under the adversarial region. A fluent liar never outperforms the human baseline in either region.

Two preregistration-time hypotheses about mechanism were tested and rejected; only magnitudes are established.

Version 2.0.0 corrects two metadata defects in 1.0.0 and changes nothing scientific. See the version note.
